lead_dispositions.canonical_boundary: Do not convert supplier revenue, a recommended-vendor qualification, an anonymous deployment example, or a product-capacity milestone into industry-wide AI-storage units/exabytes or installed-base adoption.
lead_dispositions.researcher_interpretation: The 2024 enterprise/data-center SSD demand signal is now deeper than vendor positioning alone: Micron reports a quarterly data-center SSD revenue milestone, Kioxia reports its flash-memory shipment increase was mainly in enterprise SSDs, and Micron reports an AI-platform recommended-vendor qualification. A 2023 Solidigm case also supplies a vendor-reported real workload deployment antecedent. These are distinct commercialization/adoption signals and remain non-additive because they use different measures and scopes.

lead_dispositions.canonical_boundary: The cumulative Solidigm figure is vendor-specific QLC-based product volume since 2018 and cannot be relabelled as enterprise-only, 2024-only, installed-base, industry-wide or AI-attributable exabytes. The 122TB product itself was still sampling at the November 2024 vintage.
lead_dispositions.researcher_interpretation: A real exabyte-denominated QLC shipment observation is now available: Solidigm reported more than 100EB of cumulative QLC-based product shipments since 2018. This resolves the prior absence of any quantitative QLC shipment signal at vendor scope, but it does not resolve 2024 enterprise SSD units/exabytes or AI-induced NAND demand magnitude. Kioxia's company-wide bit growth remains contextual rather than enterprise-SSD-specific.

research_compositions.summary: The evidence can be read as a bounded QLC adoption ladder: a vendor-reported CDN workload deployment in 2023, cumulative Solidigm QLC-based product shipments above 100EB by November 2024, and a new 122TB product still only sampling at that same 2024 vintage. This shows prior adoption plus continuing product-density progression without treating the new capacity milestone itself as adoption.

Micron's data-center SSD revenue milestone, Kioxia's enterprise-SSD-led flash shipment increase and Micron's GB200 recommended-vendor qualification are mutually consistent commercialization signals around data-center/AI storage in 2024, but they have no common unit denominator and do not establish an AI-only industry demand quantity.

independent_gb200_confirmation.summary: A bounded reverse search did not recover an NVIDIA source naming Micron 9550 on the GB200 NVL72 recommended-vendor list. Micron's self-statement remains usable only at supplier-reported qualification scope.

industry_wide_enterprise_ssd_units_exaby.summary: This pass found vendor-specific shipment/revenue/mix signals but no claim-scoped primary or methodological-primary industry-wide 2024 enterprise SSD unit/exabyte total. No absence claim is made.

resolved_direct_claims.summary: Solidigm cumulative QLC shipment statement and sampling stage, the vendor-reported CDN deployment case, Micron's data-center SSD revenue milestone, Kioxia's enterprise-SSD-led shipment-direction statement and company-wide bit-growth context were directly read from their owning publishers.

unresolved_questions: What was industry-wide enterprise SSD shipment volume in units and/or exabytes during 2024 on a consistent measurement basis?
How much of Solidigm's cumulative greater-than-100EB QLC-based product shipment figure is enterprise/data-center SSD rather than other QLC product scope?
What share of 2024 vendor data-center SSD revenue and shipments was attributable specifically to AI workloads versus traditional cloud/data-center recovery?
Can a named customer, platform owner or independent methodological-primary source corroborate specific 2024 QLC enterprise deployments or GB200 SSD qualification without changing the claim scope?
